dataset.name: Meteorological Conditions in Urban Sites in Knoxville, USA. 2023
description: This 2023 dataset, which contains four csv files, reports hourly air temperature, wind speed, solar radiation, incident short wave, reflected short wave, incident long wave, emitted long wave, net radiation, and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) data measured in urban parks in Knoxville, Tennessee, USA. The sites include Cumberland Estates Park (CEP), Socially Equal Energy Efficient Development (SEEED), West Hills (WHP), and Victor Ashe Park (VAP). Air temperature, wind speed and direction, and solar radiation data were obtained from a METER ATMOS 41 All-in-One Weather Station (Pullman, Washington, USA). Incident and emitted radiation (shortwave and longwave) measurements were made using an Apogee (Logan, Utah, USA) net radiometer (Model SN-500-SS). The SQ-521 Full-Spectrum Quantum sensor (Apogee Instruments, Inc) recorded the PAR. The measurement data for CEP, SEEED, and VAP started on July 1, 2023, while WHP started on August 26, 2023. All measurement ended on December 31, 2023. This work is a part of a larger study which investigates the impact of soil moisture and plant evapotranspiration on ambient temperature and relative humidity in several city parks in Knoxville, Tennessee.

measurementTechnique:
Air temperature, wind speed, and solar radiation data were obtained from a METER ATMOS 41 All-in-One Weather Station (Pullman, Washington, USA). Solar radiation is measured by a pyranometer embedded in the lip pf the rain gauge funnel at the top of the ATMOS 41W. Air temperature is monitored using thermistor. Wind speed is determined by accounting the ultrasonic signals by measuring the differences in time it takes for sound to travel back and forth between sensors. Incident and emitted radiation (shortwave and longwave) measurements were made using an Apogee (Logan, Utah, USA) net radiometer (Model SN-500-SS).
The SN-500 radiometer is a four-component net radiometer designed for continuous measurement. It uses four filtered blackbody thermopile sensors to measure the four components of net radiation. An upward-facing pyranometer and pyrgeometer pair measures the downwelling shortwave and longwave radiation. Downward facing system on the other hand measures the upwelling radiation.
The SQ-521 Full-Spectrum Quantum sensor (Apogee Instruments, Inc) recorded the PAR. The SQ-521 is single-band radiometer for the continuous measurement of PAR. This Quantum Sensor measures the photosynthetic photon flux density with nearly even sensitivity across the spectral range from 389-692 nm (PAR band is 400-700 nm).
All data are logged using ZL6 Cellular Data Logger (Meter). The raw data is uploaded to ZENTRO Cloud with 15-minute time resolution, which was then averaged to hourly data for straightforward comparison with other meteorological conditions. Missing data were tagged as -9999.
